title: Getting Started with Positron: An AI-Ready Polyglot Workflow for Data Science
abstract:
This virtual three hour workshop provides a quick start for R and Python users who are curious about Positron, Posit’s new AI-ready polyglot code editor for data science. Here, you will learn how to use Positron’s time saving features to do a typical end-to-end data science task. Along the way, you will learn how to:

  • Install packages and set up a reproducible environment
  • Connect to a database
  • Add Positron Extensions 
  • Navigate the Command Palette
  • Configure Positron to use your favorite LLM model provider
  • Write, Edit, and Debug code with Positron’s built in AI Client
  • Use an LLM to explain and translate code
  • Learn the best practices for cleaning and exploring data with LLMs
  • Publish APIs, docs, apps and more with the Posit Publisher extension

This workshop will be a good fit for you as long as you have a basic familiarity with at least one of R or Python. No installation is necessary. Posit will provide a cloud environment equipped with both Positron and the LLMs we will use during class.

title: Administering and Orchestrating Next-Gen Statistical Environments for AI and Open Source Enabled Infrastructure for Regulated Use Cases
abstract: This workshop will explore practical approaches to building reproducible, well-governed R environments for regulated pharmaceutical work. We will discuss package management, risk-based package validation, deployment options such as containers and managed platforms, and the controls needed to support traceability, change management, and production readiness. Through interactive discussion, participants will consider what a minimum viable approach looks like for administering R environments across research, development, and GxP use cases. We’ll also look at the impact of AI on regulated environments.

title: AI-Powered Clinical Reporting in R with the Pharmaverse
abstract: Modern clinical reporting workflows are evolving fast, and this workshop helps you keep pace with a practical, end-to-end approach in R. You’ll learn how to move from raw data to analysis deliverables using Pharmaverse tools, including standards-aligned SDTM preparation, efficient creation of ADaM datasets, and generation of high-quality tables, listings, and graphs (TLGs) supported by Analysis Results Datasets (ARDs). You’ll also see where AI-assisted tooling can fit naturally into the workflow to support faster iteration and reduce manual rework, without sacrificing transparency, reproducibility, or reviewability. Leave with a modular, reusable playbook for applying R to every stage of clinical reporting across your team.

title: Modern Data Science in Python
abstract:
As the data science landscape evolves, many practitioners are looking to expand their toolkit to include Python. Led by Jeroen Janssens, author of the book Python Polars: The Definitive Guide and Rich Iannone, creator of the Great Tables package, this workshop will provide a practical, hands-on introduction to an end-to-end Python workflow.

We will move beyond the basics of syntax to focus on a modern stack that prioritizes readability and performance. Using Positron as our development environment, we’ll navigate a complete project lifecycle. The workshop covers:

  • Data Manipulation: performant data wrangling using Polars.
  • Visualization: implementing the Grammar of Graphics in Python with Plotnine.
  • Reporting: creating presentation-ready tables with Great Tables.
  • Modeling: building machine learning models using Scikit-Learn.

The workshop is structured around a single case study. You’ll work through a series of exercises designed to help you get familiar with these tools. By the end of the day, you’ll have a good idea of how to translate your data science skills into a Python context and a repository of code examples to apply to future projects. 

This workshop is a great fit for those getting started with data science as well as R users who want to get their feet wet with Python for doing data science.

title: Our Modern R Workflow (ft. Positron and AI)
abstract:
This workshop is designed for data scientists who are comfortable with using R for data analysis and ready to level up their software engineering skills. Led by Hadley Wickham and Jenny Bryan, you’ll learn how to write more robust, maintainable R code while taking advantage of modern tooling (cough AI cough) that can dramatically accelerate your productivity.

We’ll cover three interconnected themes. First, you’ll learn contemporary R development practices—writing functions, organizing code into packages, testing, and documentation strategies that scale from personal projects to team collaboration. Second, we’ll explore how AI assistants like Claude Code can help you write better R code faster. Third, we’ll share practical tips for getting the most out of Positron, including features specifically designed to make R development and data exploration more fluid.

Throughout the workshop, we’ll emphasize the connections between these topics: how good development practices make AI assistance more effective, how modern tooling reduces friction so you can focus on the interesting problems, and how to build workflows that are both efficient and reproducible. You’ll leave with concrete skills you can apply immediately to your own projects.

Prerequisites: Basic familiarity with R programming (e.g. using the tidyverse). You should have written a few functions before, but don’t need any experience with package development, AI coding tools, or Positron. If you have taken a package development workshop before, you’ll learn what’s changed in our workflows, especially how we’re using AI and Positron effectively.

title: Practical Machine Learning with tidymodels
abstract:
Learn how to successfully develop Machine Learning using R. tidymodels is a complete framework that implements modeling best practices using tidyverse principles. The tidymodels framework is a collection of packages for modeling and machine learning using tidyverse principles. 

Led by Max Kuhn and Emil Hvitfeldt, this workshop will teach you core tidymodels packages to preprocess data, specify and train models, and optimize the tuning parameter. You’ll learn tidymodels syntax as well as the process of predictive modeling for tabular data. Time permitting, you’ll be introduced to basic pre-processing with recipes.

This workshop is for you if you:

  • Are comfortable using tidyverse packages to read data into R, transform and reshape data, and make a variety of graphs, and
  • Have some experience with modeling, such as linear regression, logistic regression, or tree-based models. 

While the workshop will teach some terminology and modeling philosophy, it is primarily focused on showing users how to effectively develop, iterate, and validate a machine learning model.

title: Practical Quarto: Patterns, Templates, and Tooling
abstract:
This workshop is designed for Quarto users who want to update and extend their Quarto mastery. Led by Charlotte Wickham and Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel, this workshop will introduce new features of Quarto as well as blend practical recipes with conceptual understanding, so you can both copy–paste what works and understand why it works. Rather than a linear tour of Quarto features, the workshop is organized as a collection of focused, reusable patterns—each one solving a real authoring or publishing problem you’re likely to encounter.

Themes will include:

  • Design once, use anywhere: Learn how to work effectively with light and dark modes, brands, and renderings, and how to share a consistent brand across multiple Quarto projects without duplication or fragility.
  • Build reusable structures: Use template partials to factor out repeated content and layouts, making large or long-lived projects easier to maintain and evolve.
  • Understand why Typst matters: Explore why Typst deserves a place on your radar, with concrete “quick wins” that show how it can dramatically simplify PDF generation.
  • Work productively in Positron: Pick up Positron- and Quarto-specific productivity tips, including auto-formatting with Air, and practical ways to incorporate LLMs into your Quarto workflow.
  • Master freezing and reproducibility: Demystify freeze—when to check it in to version control, when to refresh it, and how to use it intentionally to balance reproducibility, performance, and collaboration.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll have a curated set of Quarto recipes and a mental model for how the pieces fit together. You’ll leave the workshop equipped to create more polished documents, scale your workflows across projects and teams, and make deliberate, informed choices about tools, formats, and authoring strategies.

title: Programming with LLMs in R and Python
abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) offer developers unprecedented programmatic capabilities. Led by Garrick Aden-Buie and Sara Altman, this workshop will introduce ellmer (R) and chatlas (Python), Posit packages that simplify LLM API integration, handling conversation complexities and enabling seamless interactions with AI models. You’ll gain a conceptual understanding of both ecosystems, but you can choose your own adventure (R or Python) for hands-on coding sessions. 

Participants will explore system prompt design, token management, and tool calling while building familiarity with current AI technologies. The workshop demonstrates that:

  • Coding with LLMs unlocks possibilities beyond standard tools
  • No advanced AI background is required
  • Implementing AI can be both accessible and exciting

Designed for AI newcomers and experienced developers, the session covers LLM integration, Shiny web app development, and touches on advanced topics like dynamic information retrieval, context engineering, and agentic workflows. Attendees will gain hands-on experience through guided exercises, providing the confidence to start their LLM journey. As a dual-language workshop, attendees can choose hands-on practice in R or Python.

title: Virtual Session: Modeling
abstract:
This virtual session will have 4 20-minute talks!

  • AI/ML SOS IDK | Olivia Hebner and Kathryn Cronquist | Summit
    Many data scientists working in R are comfortable with regression but feel overwhelmed when getting started with machine learning. Often the challenge isn’t the algorithms, it’s knowing how to structure a clean, reproducible workflow. In this session, we’ll provide a beginner-friendly on-ramp to machine learning using tidymodels within Posit tools. Through a simple random forest example, we’ll demonstrate how data splitting, preprocessing, model specification, and evaluation fit together. Attendees will leave with a clear starting framework they can immediately apply to their own ML projects in R.
  • Nowcasting Pertussis Case Counts in Washington State | Allie Warren | Washington State Department of Health
    Pertussis is a highly contagious respiratory infection, but pertussis surveillance can lag by weeks due to delays between symptom onset and reporting and the need for case investigations, limiting timely outbreak response. Nowcasting—forecasting the present from incomplete data—addresses this gap by estimating the final case count for a given onset date. At the Washington State Department of Health, we implemented a process to track the pertussis reporting delays and used the epinowcast R package to model current pertussis case counts. Nowcasting reduced the timeframe from 9 weeks for complete data to 2 weeks for reliable estimates, improving real-time awareness of pertussis trends, which allows for earlier interventions during outbreaks.
  • Beyond Prediction: A Causal Framework using R for solving real world problems | Kimberley Isabel Orozco Cornejo | ixpantia
    Standard machine learning excels at prediction, but often fails to answer strategic questions like: "What caused this?" or "What if we intervened?". Stakeholders need causal answers, not just correlations. In "Beyond Prediction, A Causal Framework using R for solving real world problems" we'll tackle a churn scenario where predictive models give wrong advice due to Simpson's Paradox. I will demonstrate how to build a reproducible causal framework in R. Using dagitty to map assumptions and other R packages to orchestrate data simulation, attendees will learn to build an in silico laboratory. People will leave knowing how to disentangle true effects from spurious correlations to drive reliable decision-making using R.
  • Interpretable NLP for Clinical Imaging: Using tidymodels and Lasso-Regularized Text Models to Classify Pleural Effusion Impressions in R | Kaitlyn Housel | University of Pennsylvania
    Clinical imaging reports contain critical diagnostic information, but their free-text format limits large-scale analysis. This talk presents an interpretable NLP pipeline built in R using tidymodels and lasso-regularized logistic regression to classify radiology impressions for pleural effusion. To improve clinical usefulness, I developed complementary functions that extract structured signals for effusion size and loculations, reducing ambiguity and strengthening model performance. The workflow emphasizes reproducibility and auditability, combining sparse text features with domain feature engineering. Attendees will learn a practical approach for modeling clinical text and strategies for augmenting statistical models with rule-based logic.

title: Virtual Session: Practical Workflows
abstract:
There are 3 20-minute talks in this session!

  • Let Your LLM Surprise You: Inbox Insights with ellmer and Posit Connect | Konstantinos Ntentes | Posit
    What if your team received a fresh, data-backed marketing insight every morning—without anyone writing it? In this talk, I’ll walk through how ellmer connects our enterprise LLM to sales-and-marketing funnel views, and how Posit Connect and blastula turn that output into actionable, inbox-ready insights with a supporting gt table and reproducible code chunk. I’ll also share how we balance analysis guardrails with creative freedom, maintain variety across runs, why misses are still useful, and how this work fits into our team’s roadmap toward trustworthy natural-language access to complex analytics for non-coder stakeholders.
  • An R app for generating appraisals reports | Michael Morales | INTUS
    Where I work, one of the teams used to write property appraisal reports in a spreadsheet. Each one had to do the edition, formatting, calculations, pictures, in a file saved locally in their computers.
    We wanted to design an app that helped them to create the report, to just enter the parameters and pictures, and let the program do the formatting, the calculations, download the report, and saving the information into the cloud facilitating the data extraction.
    And this is how we came out with PAO, which can be translated as Platform for appraisals Online, an app written in R via shinyapps, that uses officeR, flextable, bslib, etc, connects to AWS’ S3 and RDS, to save pictures and data into databases, facilitating their daily work.
  • Positron Notebooks: Built Around How You Actually Work | Nick Strayer | Posit
    At this conference you will find no shortage of presentations on what Positron does, but I want to focus on the why of the Positron Notebook Editor. We talked to data scientists across a variety of data science teams about how they work in notebooks day to day. Those conversations shaped how we built the Positron Notebook Editor.
    The goal is the feeling you loved in RStudio, where everything you need is right at your fingertips, extended into notebooks: the features you need where they feel natural. IDE features like the interactive data explorer and kernel-aware AI assistant live right inside your notebook workflow. We'll demo the full loop live: exploring data, visualizing it, and sharing results out to stakeholders.

title: Virtual Session: Quarto, R + Python
abstract:
This virtual session will have 4 20-minute talks!

  • I Didn't Abandon R—I Added Python: My Story of Growing Without Starting Over | Bilikisu Wunmi Olatunji | R-Ladies Global/ R-Ladies Abuja
    I built my consulting career with R. It helped me deliver analyses, dashboards, reports, and models that clients trusted. Then I started seeing opportunities that were a perfect fit for my experience—but they expected Python. Like many people, I told myself I wasn't ready.
    This talk is the story of how I stopped letting a programming language define my professional identity and started building on what I already knew. Through a real consulting project—not a code walkthrough—I’ll share the practical playbook that helped me transition confidently: Wrap → Validate → Swap. Along the way, I'll show how lightweight metric contracts and golden datasets helped me keep results consistent while working across R and Python.
    You'll leave with practical ideas for expanding your opportunities, navigating mixed-language environments with confidence, and growing your career without feeling like you have to start over.
  • Combining Agentic Python Applications with R Workflows Using Posit Connect | Luis Wirth | HMS Analytical Software
    Companies rely on R for their analytical workflows, while Python now supports agentic LLM-based systems, motivating architectures that combine both ecosystems.
    This talk presents a system where a Python application acts as a frontend and an agentic orchestrator and delegates code execution to an R backend. Both applications are deployed on Posit Connect via an automatic git deployment workflow. The apps communicate via API calls, allowing the agent to trigger R-based tasks such as data wrangling, plotting, and statistical calculations. Using a real system with demo data, we focus on presenting architecture and deployment patterns and discuss benefits and tradeoffs compared to all-Python or all-R designs.
  • Shift-left for more accessibility | Björn Fisseler | FernUniversität in Hagen
    Quarto lets authors produce reports, slides, and dashboards from plain-text source files, but these outputs aren’t accessible by default. This talk presents practical workflows, tools, and design guidelines to build accessible Quarto content from the start. I cover the POUR principles, semantic document structure, accessible tables and figures, alt-text strategies for plots, and comparisons of R packages and AI-assisted approaches for generating descriptions. Attendees will leave with a checklist, examples, and methods for manual and automated accessibility testing to integrate into reproducible workflows.
  • Where Do Notebooks Come From? | Wasim Lorgat | Posit
    Quarto and Jupyter are two of the most widely used tools in computational notebooks, but they offer very different experiences. Why is that?
    This talk traces two threads of development that led to where we are today, from Donald Knuth's vision of writing code as narrative, a tradition that eventually led to Quarto, as well as John McCarthy's interactive LISP paradigm whose legacy inspired the scientific Python tools that led to Jupyter.
    These threads are now converging, with the Positron IDE at the intersection, bringing the literate program and the interactive notebook together in one environment.
    I hope this talk gives you a new way to think about the tools you use every day, and the confidence to try the ones you don't.
